title: canadian dollar edges lower bond yields jump as oil tops 100 barrel 2026 09 10
text:
TORONTO, Sept 10 (Reuters) - The Canadian dollar edged lower against the greenback on Thursday and bond yields jumped as the price ​of U.S. oil topped $100 a barrel for the first ‌time since May, adding to investor concerns about the inflation outlook.
The loonie was trading 0.1% lower at 1.3810 per U.S. dollar, or 72.41 U.S. ​cents, after moving in a range of 1.3801 to 1.3835. ​The currency has pulled back from a three-week high ⁠of 1.3757 on Tuesday as the trade war between the United ​States and Canada intensified.
